findings.title: Count does not filter out archived, deleted or inactive projects
findings.explanation: The sibling function `activeProjectNames` queries only active projects (its query is cut off in the diff, but its name and the hunk context imply a filter). This query counts every row in `projects` for the org. If the table holds archived, soft-deleted, or trial or otherwise non-billable projects, customers will be overcharged once per-project pricing starts. Apply the same predicate that defines an active or billable project (for example `archived_at IS NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL`, or `status = 'active'`). Ideally, share one definition between the two functions so they cannot drift apart. Please confirm with product or billing what counts as billable.

findings.title: Point-in-time count has no defined billing semantics
findings.explanation: The function returns the live count at call time. Projects created or deleted during the billing period, or while the invoice generator runs, change the result between calls. Invoices are not reproducible, and a retry of invoice generation could produce a different amount. Decide whether billing uses a snapshot at period end, a peak, or a proration. Then pass an `asOf` or period parameter, or persist the count on the invoice so retries stay idempotent.

findings.title: No supporting index confirmed and no tests
findings.explanation: `count(*) WHERE org_id = $1` needs an index on `projects(org_id)`, or a partial index matching the billable predicate, to stay fast for large orgs. The PR also adds no tests. A billing function needs cases for archived, deleted and other-org projects, and for an org with zero projects.

findings.title: Comment should define 'billable'
findings.explanation: 'One billable unit per project' does not say which projects qualify. Document the exact criteria next to the query so future changes to project states do not silently change invoices.

 }

+}
